title: Build Reactive Primitives
short_description: Build multiple forms of state on top of one dependency tracking system.
description: The starter already includes effect, track, and trigger so you can focus on the primitives that use that graph.
Implement pedagogical versions of reactive, ref, readonly, toRef, and toRefs while preserving identity, links, and selective notifications.
instructions: Complete reactive(target) with lazy nested conversion, proxy caching, and notification only when the value changes.
Complete ref(initialValue) so it tracks its value property and converts assigned objects into reactive state.
Complete readonly(target) as a deep view that allows reads and blocks writes.
Complete toRef(object, key, defaultValue) so its reads and writes delegate to the original property.
Complete toRefs(object) so it links existing enumerable properties and preserves array shape.
Keep resetReactivity working so each test starts with empty dependencies and caches.

hints.title: Reactive proxy
hints.body: In `get`, call `track`, read with `Reflect.get`, and pass nested objects through `reactive`. In `set`, compare the previous value with `Object.is()` before calling `trigger`.

hints.title: Stable identity
hints.body: Check `reactiveCache.get(target)` before creating a proxy and store the result in the same cache. Use a separate cache for `readonly` views.

hints.title: Ref container
hints.body: The `.value` getter should call `track(reference, "value")`. The setter compares the raw value, converts objects with `reactive`, and then calls `trigger(reference, "value")`.

hints.title: Linked references
hints.body: `toRef` does not need to store a copy: its getter returns `object[key]` and its setter assigns `object[key]`. `toRefs` creates one of these links for every key from `Object.keys(object)`.
